code.note: dirty is checked on src/ only: the app code under test

limitations: Final test set: NONE. No untouched footage exists. Every clip has been seen, scored or inspected. Stated in every report.
IMG_4874 and the kids clip were inspected repeatedly: they catch regressions, they are not clean benchmarks.
Ball-6 trained on 8 of the 10 labelled clips: its shot and detection numbers on those are in-sample.
Windows are pinned to the ones the ball-5 fixtures used; the live app picks its own with its auto-sizer.

The annotation sample was hash-locked only AFTER annotation (the lock tool did not exist yet); it is seed-deterministic and regenerating it from the seed gave a byte-identical manifest, so it was not edited in between.
Ground truth for ball position is a single AI annotator working blind to detector output; repeatability is measured and reported.
Gravity-derived and ball-width-derived scales are exploratory estimates, not a validated camera calibration.
Desktop and headless-browser timings are not phone timings.

shot_classification.alignment_caveat: Matt's lists have no shot times, so shots are paired by order, or by an alignment that rewards V2 agreement when counts differ. That flatters the rule and can move one shot either way (IMG_4874 V4: 18 of 20 here, 17 of 20 in the README, which paired by time against ball-5). Time-anchored shot truth exists only where annotated (see events).

annotator.kind: single AI visual annotator (no human second opinion yet)
annotator.protocol: Looked at gridded sheets (grid every 25 px, labels every 50) of four frames at a time, in blind id order; centre read to about 2 px against the grid; a ball is annotated when at least half of it is visible, occluded_guess when its position is inferred from context; distractors listed by type; 12 frames were repeated under new ids to measure repeatability.
annotator.repeatability_caveat: the 12 repeats were annotated in the same session by the same annotator, who had seen the earlier sheets: they are not independent of memory, so the measured repeatability is an OPTIMISTIC floor on the annotation error

detection_and_localization.note: in-sample = the clip's frames were in ball-6's training set; only out-of-sample numbers speak to unseen footage

circle_fit_independence.what: Independence test of the circle-fit (copied from tools/44-round6.mjs) against manual annotation. Seeds come from the ANNOTATION here, which the training code could not do (it seeded from ball-5's proposal and kept a circle only if it agreed with that proposal).
from_the_code: seeded by the ball-5 detector's proposal (window centred on it, search radius max(8, 0.6 x the proposal's width))
kept only if support >= 0.7 AND the circle's centre is within r + 2 px of the proposal AND its size is 0.6 to 1.9 times the proposal's: selected for agreement with the detector
cannot find a ball the detector did not propose, so it says nothing about missed balls or false positives
ball-6 was trained on boxes drawn from these circles on 8 clips

seed_stability.reading: small movement means the fit finds the same edge from different seeds (seed-independent in its estimate); a large share pulled away means it follows the seed or fails

against_manual_truth.note: errors are limited by the annotation's own repeatability

circle_fit_independence.imitation_reading: if model_vs_circle is much smaller than model_vs_truth and circle_vs_truth on the clips ball-6 trained on, but not on clips it never saw, the agreement is imitation, not independent confirmation
